subject: math
intro: I'm Ms. Rivera. Today we're planning an intro to algebraic expressions for 6th graders — the first time letters show up in math for a lot of them.

beats.narration: Framing variables as "mystery numbers" makes the first exposure feel like a game.
This covers writing, reading, and evaluating expressions where letters stand for numbers.
Two skills, write and evaluate, and both show up in the exit ticket.
beats.text: Students will be able to write expressions from verbal descriptions and evaluate them for given values of the variable.

beats.narration: The puzzle naturally creates the need for a symbol that stands for "any number."
beats.text: Number puzzle: "Think of a number, add 5, double it." Students share results and we notice a pattern in how the answers relate to the starting numbers.

beats.narration: I call out the "less than" trap directly because it's the most common error I see.
beats.text: Translate phrases into expressions with a word bank (sum, product, less than, quotient). Model the tricky ones: "5 less than n" is n − 5, not 5 − n. Then evaluate 2n + 3 for n = 4.

beats.narration: The card game gives lots of repetitions quickly, and the extension keeps fast finishers thinking.
beats.text: Expression matching card game: students match verbal phrases, expressions, and values in groups of three. Early finishers create their own cards for the class.

beats.narration: One question checks both halves of the objective.
beats.text: Write an expression for "3 more than twice a number," then evaluate it when the number is 7.

outro: Puzzle, model, practice, check. Now it's your turn to plan.
